links.passage: It is one of the common irrigation scheduling methods in regions with stable sunny summer conditions (Gardner et al., 1992a,b, see also Table S1) and proved as reliable in terms of yield and water savings as more expensive soil water-based irrigation techniques (Stegman, 1986; Steele et al., 1994, 2000; Shae et al., 1999).
supporting_passages: Soon after its introduction, CWSIe became the most commonly used thermal drought stress index (Jackson et al., 1988; Gardner et al., 1992a), which it has remained ever since.
In the empirical or baseline approach, the data input is limited to Ta, δe, and Tc.
links.inference_note: The preceding sentence identifies 'it' as CWSIe, the thermal (infrared-thermometer/thermal-imaging) crop water stress index computed from canopy temperature, so the yield-reliability claim is attributed to thermal remote sensing-based scheduling.
